title: Taiwanese American Citizens League
content_html:
The Taiwanese American Citizens League (TACL) is a national 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization established on July 13, 1985 by Li-Pei Wu. Founded to promote the rights and welfare of Taiwanese Americans and foster active participation in American civic life, TACL modeled its approach on the Japanese American Citizens League (JACL), which had demonstrated how a minority community could build institutional credibility and political voice. TACL is run entirely by unpaid volunteers.

TACL’s work is organized around four pillars: Leadership, Identity, Networking, and Citizenship. Its programs serve community members of all ages, with particular emphasis on leadership and identity development for youth. Signature programs include the Leadership Identity Development (LID) Camp, Leading Youth Forward (LYF) Camp, the Political Internship Program (PIP), the Journalism Internship Program (JIP), the Entertainment Internship (EI), a High School Scholarship, and the Junior Taiwanese American Students Association (JTASA).

The organization’s professional network, Taiwanese American Professionals (TAP), was first established in 1991 with a single chapter in Los Angeles. Re-launched as a formal TACL program in 2001, TAP has grown into the largest network of young Taiwanese American professionals in the United States, with ten chapters in Atlanta, Austin, Boston, Los Angeles, New York, Orange County, San Diego, San Francisco, Seattle, and Washington D.C. TAP chapters serve as TACL’s local voice and leadership in each region, offering programs centered on professional development, cultural engagement, community service, and social networking.

Over its four decades, TACL has been active in civic advocacy, organizing nationwide Taiwanese write-in campaigns for the 1990, 2010, and 2020 US Census, advocating for hate crime protections, and challenging racially insensitive commercial practices. In 2021, TACL launched SPARK Accel, a virtual accelerator for Taiwanese American entrepreneurs.

Source: tacl.org/about, tacl.org/our-history
